caption: How hi compute works. You, or your agent, run one set of commands on your machine: hi compute run, up, or serve. hi picks the provider, checks the hardware name before calling it, confirms paid hardware, and gives every machine a time limit. It drives each provider through that provider's own CLI or API, with your sign-in, and hardware names and prices stay the provider's. The provider starts a run, which ends when its command finishes, or an instance, which stays until you stop it or it reaches its limit.

items.title: hi compute up --gpu G4
items.does: Picks the provider, checks the hardware name before calling it, asks before paid hardware, and sets `--max`.

items.title: Colab CLI · HF Jobs · RunPod · Shadeform
items.does: hi drives each one through its own CLI or REST API; `--dry-run` shows the exact call.

items.title: t4-3fa1
items.does: Runs your script or command and ends with it; `hi compute logs` follows it.

items.title: box
items.does: Stays until you stop it or it reaches `--max`: ssh, a tunnel, a notebook, a model server.

key.text: Where hi runs; you use the rented machine as if it were local.
The same commands for every provider, with a check before anything costs money.
hi hides each provider's tool, but not its hardware names or prices.
A run ends with its command; an instance ends when you stop it. Both end at their limit.
